Prevention: Eliminating crop residue could reduce the occurrence of overwintering and discourage inoculation in subsequent seasons.
Application of nitrogen based fertilizer on the actual requirements of the crop may control blast epidemics.
Maintain plant to plant distance of 9in, i.e, 15 to 20 plants per square feet.
Get the field free from weeds and alternate hosts.
Monitoring: Rice blast can infect all parts of the plant including roots.
During early stage of heading, monitor 2-3 times a week.
Scout for leaf symptoms beginning at seedling stage and continue into heading stage.
Watch for flagleaf collar symptoms on early-planted susceptible varieties.
Look for diamond shaped lesions on the leaves.
Lesions on the sheaths are relatively rare.
On collars, look for a general area of necrosis at the union of the two tissues.
Look for rotten neck or blanking.
On panicles, look for gray brown discolorations of the branches of the panicle.
Direct Control: Bipolaris sorokiniana were found to reduce blast when sprayed on plants.
Saccharomyces cerevisiae can minimize infection by inhibiting production of appressorium (fungus body).
Maintain proper flood level for rice to grow.
